doi_status_legend.verified: Crossref title match >= 0.90 and container consistent
doi_status_legend.preprint: Crossref best match is a preprint version; journal DOI unconfirmed
doi_status_legend.unverified: No confident Crossref match; cite by PMID only

entries.title: Music and binaural beat interventions for young adults: A systematic review of effects on anxiety, sleep, and cognition

outcomes.note: most studies improved at least one domain; reported SMD range 0.3-0.6

findings: Heterogeneous designs and small samples limit certainty
Interventions included bedtime music, audiovisual stimulation and binaural beats
entries.product_use: Relaxation/sleep hygiene framing only; no cognitive-enhancement claim

entries.title: Efficacy of theta binaural beat therapy on pain, cognition and anxiety in adults: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials

outcomes.note: not poolable; anxiolytic effects in procedural and chronic pain contexts
theta entrainment favoured episodic memory in some trials

findings: Quantitative synthesis was only possible for pain
Authors describe the intervention as promising, safe and low-cost
entries.product_use: Theta audio may support relaxation; do not claim memory enhancement

entries.title: Binaural beats for perioperative anxiety and pain: A systematic review and meta-analysis

outcomes.note: systolic blood pressure mmHg; heart rate -3.37 bpm

findings: Binaural beats outperformed non-binaural audio on anxiety and pain
Heterogeneity was substantial
entries.product_use: Anxiety/pain context is the strongest audio signal; cognition is not

entries.title: The effects of music and auditory stimulation on autonomic arousal, cognition and attention: A systematic review

outcomes.note: cardiac, electrodermal and pupil measures mixed or insufficient
arousal and cognition usually studied separately

findings: Evidence for the arousal-mood hypothesis is at best indirect
Music, noise and binaural beats show mixed autonomic effects
entries.product_use: Do not build an arousal-mediation claim without your own measurement

entries.title: Efficacy of binaural auditory beats in cognition, anxiety, and pain perception: a meta-analysis

outcomes.note: overall across memory, attention, anxiety and analgesia
direction and magnitude depend on frequency, exposure time and timing

findings: 35 effect sizes
Exposure before and during the task outperformed during-task only
Longer exposure was associated with larger effects
Masking with noise was not necessary
limitations: Pooled across cognition, anxiety and pain
entries.product_use: A binaural preset is a parameter set, not a protocol; expose frequency and duration

entries.title: Auditory beat stimulation and its effects on cognition and mood states

outcomes.note: auditory steady-state responses and neurophysiological changes summarised

findings: Stimulation parameters are central to the design
The literature contains contradictory outcomes
entries.product_use: Any entrainment claim must specify frequency, duration and timing

entries.title: Effectiveness of technology-assisted nonpharmacological interventions for cognitive impairment in older adults: A systematic review and network meta-analysis
findings: VR cognitive training ranked best for cognition
Robot-based cognitive and social training ranked best for depressive symptoms
limitations: Very high heterogeneity for global cognition
Certainty claim is higher than comparable reviews
entries.product_use: Technology-assisted formats are plausible; certainty should be downgraded for inconsistency

entries.title: Cognitive training in neurological disorders: meta-analytic evidence for behavioral gains and neural correlates

outcomes.note: increased bilateral precuneus and left precentral gyrus activation; only precuneus tracked behaviour

findings: Adaptive training showed reduced left precentral activation versus fixed difficulty
Training dose was not a significant moderator
entries.product_use: Adaptivity has a mechanistic rationale but not a demonstrated behavioural advantage here

entries.title: Comparative efficacy of executive function interventions for Chinese children with neurodevelopmental disorders: A network meta-analysis
findings: Statistically significant but very small effects
Authors call for large-scale long-term validation
limitations: Very small effects of uncertain clinical meaning
entries.product_use: Statistical significance is not user-visible benefit; set a minimum meaningful effect

entries.title: Effects of Pure Cognitive Training on Gait and Balance in Older Adults: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

outcomes.note: dual-task gait speed, high-quality studies, n=376

findings: Cognitive training improves dual-task but not single-task walking
Effective protocol was 40-60 minutes, 2-3 times weekly for 8-10 weeks
entries.product_use: Dual-task paradigms are the defensible bridge from cognition to everyday function

entries.title: The asymmetry of working memory training transfer: A systematic review and meta-analysis

outcomes.note: updating training to span tasks, p<.001
span training to updating tasks, p=.453

findings: Transfer is asymmetric and tracks cognitive demand, not only task similarity
Updating training also transferred to non-working-memory outcomes
Effects were larger at lower training doses, in non-adult samples, and with verbal stimuli
limitations: Three-level model but most trials small
Dose finding contradicts a simple more-is-better assumption
entries.product_use: Design demand and task-general ability into the progression, not just surface similarity

entries.title: Cognitive transfer and durability of computerised cognitive training in older adults with mild cognitive impairment: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials

outcomes.note: excluding Wu et al. gives g=0.00 (95% CI -0.26 to 0.25)

findings: No included trial was at overall low risk of bias
Functional far-transfer evidence was low certainty and limited
entries.product_use: Central caution: do not promise durable far transfer in MCI

entries.title: The effect of cognitive training on children with attention deficit and hyperactivity disorder: A meta-analysis
findings: Benefit for attention and executive function, not hyperactivity/impulsivity
Longer training (>30 days) was associated with larger attention effects
entries.product_use: Never market as ADHD treatment; at most an adjunct with clinician oversight

entries.title: Cognitive and behavioural rehabilitation interventions for survivors of childhood cancer with neurocognitive sequelae: A systematic review

outcomes.note: possible visual attention benefit for those with WM impairment
evidence did not support far transfer to real life
no significant near or far transfer for neurofeedback and exergaming

findings: Highest-quality RCTs covered Cogmed, neurofeedback and exergaming
Only near transfer was supported, and only for working memory
entries.product_use: Direct evidence that near transfer does not imply real-life benefit

entries.title: Cognitive Training During Midlife: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
findings: Six training types and six cognitive domains were clustered
Benefits were domain-specific and modest
entries.product_use: Midlife healthy adults are a plausible but under-studied target

entries.title: The efficacy of cognitive stimulation, cognitive training, and cognitive rehabilitation for people living with dementia: a systematic review and meta-analysis

outcomes.note: group and individual cognitive stimulation effective at any severity; individual and group CT effective in mild dementia
cognitive rehabilitation improved functional abilities in mild dementia
cognitive rehabilitation most effective for caregiver outcomes

findings: Effectiveness differs by dementia severity and intervention form
Heterogeneity was high
limitations: High clinical, statistical and methodological heterogeneity
Guideline-based review, not a product trial
entries.product_use: Clinical use must be severity-stratified and supervised

entries.title: Impact of Non-Pharmacological Cognitive Interventions on Real-World Daily Function in Children With Cancer: A Systematic Review

outcomes.note: reported range Cohen d 0.28-0.87 across Cogmed trials
reported range Cohen d -0.36 to -0.98 for inattention in daily life
4 of 6 Cogmed trials showed functional benefits; other interventions insufficiently studied

findings: Functional benefits were reported for some Cogmed trials
Less than half reported personalisation, fidelity or cost
entries.product_use: Real-world function is measurable but rarely measured well

entries.title: Virtual Reality Interventions for Older Adults With Mild Cognitive Impairment: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials

outcomes.note: very small effects on daily living, depression, gait and balance

findings: VR without therapist involvement improved memory and attention
Immersive VR improved attention and executive function
entries.product_use: Domain-specific gains are achievable without a therapist present

entries.title: Efficacy of digital therapeutic applications for cognitive training among older adults with mild cognitive impairment or dementia: A systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
findings: Only 10 RCTs entered the network
Effects are large and should be treated cautiously given the network size
limitations: No certainty rating reported in the abstract
entries.product_use: Intensive digital CCT is a candidate high-dose protocol, pending certainty assessment

entries.journal: Journal of Prevention of Alzheimer's Disease
entries.title: Comparative efficacy of cognitive training modalities in cognitive impairment: A systematic review and network meta-analysis

outcomes.note: cognitive strategy training superior to active or passive control
reminiscence therapy ranked highest in network

findings: No significant moderation by severity, delivery format, interventionist expertise, training duration or control type
Reminiscence therapy ranked best for global cognition
limitations: Ranking is not proof of superiority
entries.product_use: Duration alone is not a reliable efficacy lever; content and strategy matter

entries.title: Effects of Serious Games on Memory Improvement in Older Adults Without Obvious Cognitive Impairment: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
findings: Cognitive training games SMD 0.42; exergames SMD 0.22
Blank control and active control both yielded SMD 0.35
entries.product_use: Game framing is not itself evidence of efficacy; design for domain-specific challenge

entries.title: The Effectiveness of Computerized Cognitive Training in Patients With Poststroke Cognitive Impairment: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

outcomes.note: memory, language and motor function limited

findings: Short-term high-frequency training was more effective than long-term low-frequency training
A structured maintenance plan is recommended
entries.product_use: Rehabilitation-adjacent, supervised positioning only; not a wellness claim

entries.title: Efficacy of different digital interventions in patients with mild cognitive impairment or dementia: A systematic review and network meta-analysis
findings: Mobile video games and immersive VR ranked best
Pooled magnitudes are not usable for planning
limitations: Implausible effect sizes indicate a scaling or data-extraction problem
entries.product_use: Direction only; exclude from dose or effect-size planning

entries.title: Cogmed cognitive training for working memory: a systematic review and meta-analysis

outcomes.note: significant small immediate verbal and visuospatial WM gain
small sustained verbal WM benefit at 2-6 months; no difference <2 months

findings: Commercial working-memory training shows short-term near transfer in adults
Sustained evidence is limited
entries.product_use: Expect near transfer; treat far transfer as unproven

entries.title: Effect of Cognitive Training on Cancer-Related Cognitive Impairment in Patients With Breast Cancer: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

outcomes.note: FACT-Cog global; source reports SMD=0.2 with 95% CI -0.39 to -0.01; sign normalized
source reports SMD=0.39 with 95% CI -0.58 to -0.19; sign normalized

findings: Funnel plots suggested possible publication bias
Authors rate the evidence low quality
entries.product_use: Same modality, different population; do not generalise across clinical groups

entries.title: Effectiveness of computerised cognitive training on cognitive functioning and quality of life in cancer survivors with cancer-related cognitive impairments: A systematic review and meta-analysis
findings: Small but consistent executive and working-memory gains
Mobile and tablet delivery is suggested for engagement
entries.product_use: A credible adjunct niche with modest, domain-specific effects

entries.title: Effectiveness of VR-based cognitive training and games on cognitive rehabilitation in patients with MCI: a systematic review and meta-analysis
findings: Immersion level was a significant moderator
Games showed a trend toward larger effects than training
limitations: Immersion and cybersickness not fully reported
entries.product_use: Immersive delivery needs tolerance screening and comfort controls

entries.title: Treatment Response Following Adaptive PASAT Training for Depression Vulnerability: a Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

outcomes.note: small significant effect post-training and at follow-up
small significant effect; larger in non-healthy populations

findings: Number of sessions did not moderate the effect
Largest benefits in at-risk, remitted and clinically depressed groups
entries.product_use: A narrow cognitive-control protocol can affect mood, but dose is unresolved

entries.title: Network meta-analysis of the effects of different cognitive trainings on the cognitive function of patients with mild cognitive impairment
findings: Neuropsychological training ranked best overall
Interventions longer than 8 weeks were more effective
limitations: Network geometry not reported in abstract
entries.product_use: Content-specific training and >=8-week programmes are reasonable defaults

entries.title: Evaluation of Computerized Cognitive Training and Cognitive and Daily Function in Patients Living With HIV: A Meta-analysis
findings: Six of eight domains improved
Daily function improved with a small-to-moderate effect
entries.product_use: Clinical rehabilitation can show broader effects than healthy-adult training

entries.title: Working Memory Training Does Not Improve Performance on Measures of Intelligence or Other Measures of Far Transfer: Evidence From a Meta-Analytic Review

outcomes.note: intermediate transfer to verbal and visuospatial working memory
no reliable far transfer against treated controls
decoding, reading comprehension and arithmetic did not improve

findings: 145 experimental comparisons
Gain on working-memory measures was not related to far-transfer magnitude
No evidential value under treated controls
limitations: DOI unconfirmed in Crossref; cited by PMID
Treated-control designs were scarce in the primary literature
entries.product_use: Never claim intelligence or academic gains from working-memory training

entries.journal: Psychological Science in the Public Interest
entries.title: Do "Brain-Training" Programs Work?

outcomes.note: extensive evidence of improvement on trained tasks
less evidence for closely related tasks and little for distantly related tasks
little evidence that training improves everyday cognitive performance

findings: No cited industry study conformed to all best practices
Design and analysis shortcomings preclude definitive conclusions
limitations: Reviewed studies cited by brain-training companies, not a full systematic search
entries.product_use: Best-practice standards are the product's evidence bar, not a marketing footnote

entries.title: Improving fluid intelligence with training on working memory: a meta-analysis

outcomes.note: small but significant effect of n-back training on fluid intelligence

findings: Only n-back studies in healthy adults aged 18-50
Several moderators were identified
entries.product_use: A small fluid-intelligence signal exists but is fragile and paradigm-specific

entries.journal: Journal of the American Geriatrics Society
entries.title: Ten-year effects of the advanced cognitive training for independent and vital elderly cognitive training trial on cognition and everyday functioning in older adults

outcomes.note: memory training on IADL at 10 years; 99% CI
speed of processing maintained at 10 years
reasoning maintained; memory no longer maintained

findings: 60% of trained participants versus 50% of controls were at or above baseline IADL at 10 years
Effects on targeted abilities persisted for reasoning and speed but not memory
entries.product_use: Durability is possible for reasoning and speed, not for memory

entries.title: Is working memory training effective? A meta-analytic review

outcomes.note: verbal working-memory gain not sustained at follow-up
no convincing generalization to nonverbal ability, verbal ability, inhibition, decoding or arithmetic

findings: 30 group comparisons from 23 studies
Short-term specific training effects do not generalise
limitations: Mixed clinical and typically developing samples
entries.product_use: Treat near transfer as the default expectation and far transfer as unproven

entries.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
entries.title: Improving fluid intelligence with training on working memory

outcomes.note: transfer to fluid intelligence; gain depended on training dose

findings: The trained task differed from the intelligence test
More training produced larger gains
limitations: Later meta-analyses with treated controls did not replicate far transfer
entries.product_use: Historical landmark only; do not plan a product on this result

entries.title: A meta-analysis of cognitive remediation in schizophrenia
findings: Effects on psychosocial functioning were stronger when cognitive remediation was paired with psychiatric rehabilitation
Cognitive remediation alone improved cognition but not function as much
entries.product_use: Functional benefit requires a rehabilitation context, not a game alone

entries.title: Long-term effects of cognitive training on everyday functional outcomes in older adults

outcomes.note: reasoning training on IADL at 5 years; 99% CI

findings: ACTIVE trial, 5-year follow-up
Booster training improved everyday speed in the speed group
entries.product_use: Reasoning-style training is the most defensible far-transfer candidate in older adults

entries.journal: Journal of the American Academy of Child & Adolescent Psychiatry
entries.title: Computerized training of working memory in children with ADHD--a randomized, controlled trial

outcomes.note: span-board task improved post-intervention and at 3 months

findings: Multicentre double-blind trial
44 of 53 met the compliance criterion
entries.product_use: Near transfer and parent-rated change can coexist without far transfer

entries.journal: Journal of Clinical and Experimental Neuropsychology
entries.title: Training of working memory in children with ADHD

outcomes.note: head movements during a computerized test reduced

findings: Double-blind, placebo-controlled design
A second experiment showed similar gains in young adults without ADHD
limitations: Later reviews did not confirm broad far transfer
entries.product_use: Hypothesis-generating; not a basis for a product claim

entries.title: Gamification and Language Learning to Enhance Cognition in Older Adults: A Systematic Literature Review

outcomes.note: results lean toward improvement after gamified cognitive training, especially in Asian samples

findings: Findings were mixed, especially for language learning
Gamified cognitive training was more consistent than language learning
entries.product_use: Gamification is a delivery layer, not a mechanism

entries.title: Exergame-Based Behavior Change Interventions for Promoting Physical Activity: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Studies
findings: Behaviour-change technique count moderated effectiveness
Goal setting, action planning, self-monitoring and instruction were the most used techniques
entries.product_use: Engagement design should use explicit behaviour-change techniques, not points alone

entries.title: Effects of non-pharmacological interventions in patients with cancer-related cognitive impairment: A meta-analysis
findings: Several interventions improved subjective or objective cognition
Heterogeneity was substantial and certainty low
limitations: Multi-intervention review, not a combination trial
entries.product_use: Cancer-related cognitive impairment is a multi-intervention space; do not attribute effects to one modality

entries.title: Comparative efficacy and acceptability of pharmacological, psychological, and neurostimulatory interventions for ADHD in adults: a systematic review and component network meta-analysis

outcomes.note: cognitive remediation, clinician-report only; very imprecise

findings: Only stimulants and atomoxetine improved core symptoms on both self- and clinician-rated measures
Non-pharmacological effects were inconsistent across raters
Neurofeedback and neurostimulation evidence covered only 10 RCTs and 194 participants
limitations: Non-pharmacological trials were few and often unblinded
entries.product_use: The strongest ADHD comparator evidence does not support a neurofeedback product claim

entries.title: Network meta-analysis of the effects of long-term non-pharmacologic treatment on inhibitory control in children and adolescents with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder

outcomes.note: physical exercise ranked best at post-test
behaviour therapy ranked best at follow-up
neurofeedback improved post-test inhibition but had no significant long-term effect

findings: Exercise, cognitive training, behaviour therapy and neurofeedback all improved inhibitory control post-test
Maintenance was best for behaviour therapy and cognitive training
Neurofeedback effects diminished over time
entries.product_use: Immediate task gains fade; maintenance must be designed and measured

entries.title: A systematic review and network meta-analysis comparing various non-pharmacological treatments for older people with mild cognitive impairment

outcomes.note: cognitive stimulation and cognitive rehabilitation had no significant effect

findings: Physical exercise had the best ranking
Cognitive stimulation and rehabilitation were not significant in this network
entries.product_use: A direct counter-signal: exercise may outperform cognitive stimulation in MCI networks

entries.title: Efficacy of non-pharmacological interventions on executive functions in children and adolescents with ADHD: A systematic review and meta-analysis
findings: Physical exercise, cognitive training and an EF-specific curriculum showed the largest effects
Most outcomes were neurocognitive tasks, not blinded ratings
limitations: Effect sizes are too large to be credible
entries.product_use: Do not use these magnitudes; task-based EF gains are not everyday function

entries.title: Evaluating the cognitive impact of exergames on community-dwelling older adults beyond laboratory settings: a systematic review and meta-analysis
findings: Small overall effect in community settings
Domain-specific effects did not reach significance
Clinical populations remain limited
limitations: Small effect at the edge of clinical relevance
entries.product_use: Exergame benefit is small; do not promise transformation

entries.title: Effectiveness of different digital interventions on symptoms for children and adolescents with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder: a network meta-analysis
findings: Neurofeedback had the highest SUCRA for inattention (79.4%)
Computer-based cognitive tasks ranked best for hyperactivity/impulsivity
Mobile gaming ranked best for executive function
entries.product_use: Digital delivery can move parent/teacher ratings; that is not blinded efficacy

entries.journal: Journal of the American Medical Directors Association
entries.title: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Combined Cognitive and Physical Interventions on Cognition Function in Frail Older Adults
findings: Large pooled effects in a small, frail sample
Long-term follow-up is missing
entries.product_use: Frailty is a distinct population requiring supervised, low-risk delivery

entries.title: Digital Physical Exercise Interventions for Cognitive Functions in Older Adults: Systematic Review and Bayesian Network Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
findings: Cumulative training >=1000 minutes was associated with more stable memory benefit
Certainty was very low for most comparisons
limitations: Unclear allocation concealment and suspected reporting bias
entries.product_use: Movement plus cognition is promising; dose >=1000 minutes is a design hypothesis

entries.title: A meta-analysis of the effects of combined interventions centered on cognitive training on cognition, executive function, and negative emotions in patients with Alzheimer's disease

outcomes.note: cognitive training plus non-invasive brain stimulation ranked first
cognitive plus exercise vs physical exercise alone; implausibly large

findings: Combined interventions were superior to single modalities in the network
Cognitive plus exercise ranked best for executive function and negative emotions
limitations: Effect size magnitude is not credible
entries.product_use: Do not use these magnitudes for planning; the direction is hypothesis-generating only

entries.title: Systematic review and meta-analysis of the effects of combined physical and cognitive training on depression symptoms in adults across clinical populations
findings: Most comparisons were against physical training alone
The effect disappeared when restricted to depression-specific measures
entries.product_use: Mood benefits are not robust enough for a depression claim

entries.title: Optimal dose and type of non-pharmacological treatments to improve cognitive function in people with Alzheimer's disease: a systematic review and network meta-analysis

outcomes.note: tDCS, physical exercise and rTMS ranked highest; cognitive stimulation, cognitive training, multidisciplinary programme and reminiscence also significant
non-linear dose-response for tDCS, exercise, rTMS, cognitive stimulation and cognitive training

findings: A minimum clinically relevant dose was estimated for tDCS and exercise but not for cognitive training
Low-dose exercise improved cognition
entries.product_use: Dose-response must be measured, not assumed, per modality

entries.journal: Journal of Stroke and Cerebrovascular Diseases
entries.title: Exergames for rehabilitation in stroke survivors: Umbrella review of meta-analyses
findings: Intervention duration varied from 1 to 16 weeks
Nintendo Wii dominated the evidence base
entries.product_use: Exergames are a rehabilitation tool; cognition is a secondary outcome

entries.title: The Effects of Exergaming on the Depressive Symptoms of People With Dementia: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

outcomes.note: source reports SMD=1.46 with 95% CI -2.50 to -0.43; sign normalized to negative for improvement

findings: All studies showed a trend of improvement
Risk of bias was moderate to serious
entries.product_use: Do not build a depression claim on six studies

entries.title: Enhancing effects of exercise and neurofeedback: A systematic review and meta-analysis of computer game-based interventions for pediatric ADHD

outcomes.note: physical exercise/VR subgroup; improved both inattention and hyperactivity/impulsivity

findings: Social components and plain game elements did not show significant effects
Dose and demographics did not moderate effects
entries.product_use: Combination hypotheses are weak; do not treat them as additive certainty

entries.title: Effects of motor-cognitive training on cognitive function and gait performance in older adults with dementia: a systematic review and meta-analysis

outcomes.note: no significant improvement in memory, attention or executive function

findings: Motor-cognitive training outperformed physical or cognitive training alone for global cognition and single-task gait
Domain-specific cognitive tests did not improve
limitations: Global cognition composite may drive the result
entries.product_use: Composite improvement without domain improvement is a measurement warning

entries.title: Effects of different exercise modalities on balance performance in healthy older adults: a systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials

outcomes.note: exergame ranked best on Berg Balance Scale
Wii Fit ranked best for Timed Up and Go

findings: Traditional balance training, mind-body interventions and Otago were also effective
Exergame and augmented reality can be cautiously considered
entries.product_use: Movement safety outcomes can be measured even when cognition is the goal

entries.title: Single-domain and multidomain lifestyle interventions for the prevention of cognitive decline in older adults who are cognitively unimpaired: a systematic review and network meta-analysis

outcomes.note: physical exercise plus cognitive training vs health education

findings: Combining physical exercise and cognitive training had the strongest effect
Adding more domains did not automatically increase benefit
40% of studies were at high risk of bias and publication bias was suggested
limitations: Global cognition only as primary outcome
High risk of bias in 44 studies
entries.product_use: Pair cognitive work with movement; do not assume more modalities is better

entries.title: The efficacy of combining cognitive training and noninvasive brain stimulation: A transdiagnostic systematic review and meta-analysis

outcomes.note: learning/memory vs CT alone, post-intervention; not sustained
seven other cognitive domains, symptoms and everyday functioning did not benefit

findings: Only 4 of 72 studies had low risk of bias in all domains
Many studies lacked blinded assessors or trainers
limitations: NIBS has no consumer-safe role in a general platform
entries.product_use: Do not add brain stimulation to a consumer product on this evidence

entries.title: Combined exercise and cognitive interventions for adults with mild cognitive impairment and dementia: A systematic review and network meta-analysis

outcomes.note: delayed recall superior to exercise alone
not superior to cognitive intervention alone on any outcome

findings: Combination beats exercise alone on some cognitive outcomes
Combination does not beat cognitive training alone
Synergy is not established
entries.product_use: Adding movement helps versus movement alone, not versus good cognitive training

entries.title: A 2 year multidomain intervention of diet, exercise, cognitive training, and vascular risk monitoring versus control to prevent cognitive decline in at-risk elderly people (FINGER): a randomised controlled trial

outcomes.note: between-group difference in NTB total Z score change per year
46 (7%) intervention vs 6 (1%) control; musculoskeletal pain 32 (5%) vs none

findings: Large, long-term multidomain prevention trial
Effect is statistically significant but very small
Exercise component carried musculoskeletal adverse events
limitations: Multidomain bundle cannot isolate the cognitive component
entries.product_use: Multimodal prevention works at population scale, not as a dramatic individual gain

entries.title: Nonpharmacological interventions for ADHD: systematic review and meta-analyses of randomized controlled trials of dietary and psychological treatments

outcomes.note: psychological treatments, raters closest to the setting; range 0.40-0.64
attenuated to non-significance with the best probably blinded assessment, except free fatty acids and food-colour exclusion

findings: 54 of 2,904 screened records included
Blinding attenuates psychological treatment effects
limitations: Dietary and psychological treatments analysed together
entries.product_use: Blinded outcomes are the only credible basis for an ADHD-adjacent claim

entries.title: Modulating complex brain states using MVPA-based neurofeedback: A systematic review

outcomes.note: moderate neural effect, particularly emotion regulation

findings: Neural modulation is more reproducible than behavioural change
Methodological standardisation is lacking
entries.product_use: Neural change alone must never be marketed as cognitive improvement

entries.title: Effects of EEG neurofeedback in adults with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder: a systematic review of randomised and non-randomised studies

outcomes.note: RCTs showed small, generally non-significant effects; naturalistic and personalised studies reported large reductions

findings: Cognitive improvements were inconsistent and largely attributable to practice effects
Electrophysiological changes were protocol-specific
entries.product_use: Naturalistic pre-post gains are not efficacy evidence

entries.title: Neurofeedback for Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

outcomes.note: probably blinded total symptom reports, k=20, n=1214
restricted to established standard protocols, k=9, n=681
only significant neuropsychological outcome of five

findings: No clinically meaningful group-level benefit when reports are probably blinded
Standard protocols and processing speed are the remaining signals
entries.product_use: Anchor claim: consumer neurofeedback is not an ADHD treatment

entries.title: Can Electroencephalography-Based Neurofeedback Treat Post-traumatic Stress Disorder? A Meta-analysis Study

outcomes.note: significant reduction post-intervention and at 1 and 3 months; sham-controlled sub-analysis supported the effect

findings: Excluding two outlying studies removed heterogeneity
Target frequency, region and feedback modality were confounded by publication year
entries.product_use: Clinical PTSD use requires supervised trials, not a consumer app

entries.title: Music in the loop: a systematic review of current neurofeedback methodologies using music

outcomes.note: no consensus on imaging or behavioural measures of neurofeedback success

findings: Mechanistic explanations for music-based feedback are lacking
The emotional link between music and brain activity is asserted more than demonstrated
entries.product_use: Aesthetic feedback is a design choice, not evidence of mechanism

entries.title: Consumer-Grade Neurofeedback With Mindfulness Meditation: Meta-Analysis

outcomes.note: no mechanistic modulation of brain targets in RCTs or within-participant designs

findings: Most studies used the Muse device
Effects may reflect neurosuggestion or placebo
19 of 21 studies did not assess adverse effects
entries.product_use: Consumer EEG must be framed as a feedback/awareness tool, not a brain-training cure

entries.journal: Scandinavian Journal of Medicine & Science in Sports
entries.title: The Effect of EEG Neurofeedback Training on Sport Performance: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

outcomes.note: above-median CRED-nf quality; larger than lower-quality studies

findings: Higher methodological quality was associated with larger effects, which is atypical
CRED-nf reporting gaps remain
limitations: Effect increases with quality is unusual and needs replication
entries.product_use: Peak-performance claims need independent replication first

entries.title: Comparative effectiveness of electroencephalogram-neurofeedback training of 3-45 frequency band on memory in healthy population: a network meta-analysis with systematic literature search

outcomes.note: alpha plus working-memory training vs active control; implausible magnitude

findings: Alpha band (7-13 Hz) ranked highest for both memory types
No publication bias detected
limitations: Working-memory effect size is not credible and suggests scaling or network problems
entries.product_use: Alpha is a plausible target; the magnitude is not usable for planning

entries.title: Comparative efficacy of neurofeedback, tDCS, and TMS: The future of therapy for adults with ADHD. A systematic review and meta-analysis

outcomes.note: meta-analysis did not reach significance for neurofeedback, tDCS or rTMS

findings: Neurofeedback lacked study quality
The authors still call it a possible option for people unwilling to undergo neuromodulation
entries.product_use: Preference-sensitive option, not an efficacy claim

entries.title: Neurofeedback training for executive function in ADHD children: a systematic review and meta-analysis
findings: Dose above 1260 minutes was associated with larger inhibition and working-memory effects
Effects on working memory were more durable
entries.product_use: Do not resolve the conflict by choosing the favourable review; report both

entries.title: Systematic review and meta-analysis of neurofeedback and its effect on posttraumatic stress disorder
findings: Effect increased at follow-up
Authors attribute the effect to newer fMRI-guided neurofeedback and its derivates
entries.product_use: Do not generalise fMRI-guided findings to consumer EEG

entries.title: Modulation of human frontal midline theta by neurofeedback: A systematic review and quantitative meta-analysis

outcomes.note: confidence interval crosses zero; substantial heterogeneity Q(16)=167.43

findings: Sub-analysis supported frontal midline theta upregulation
Authors note high design heterogeneity
entries.product_use: Learning a brain target is not the same as a cognitive benefit

entries.title: Uncovering the power of neurofeedback: a meta-analysis of its effectiveness in treating major depressive disorders
findings: Longer interventions were associated with better symptom and neuropsychological outcomes
Shorter sessions were associated with better neurophysiological outcomes
entries.product_use: Depression is a clinical indication requiring care pathways

entries.title: Neurofeedback Training in Children with ADHD: A Systematic Review of Personalization and Methodological Features Facilitating Training Conditions

outcomes.note: three personalised studies showed short- and long-term improvements; only 3 of 109 studies met criteria

findings: Individual alpha peak frequency personalisation is promising but based on three studies
Feedback animations, timing, self-control instructions and medication dose were associated with success
limitations: Personalisation is a hypothesis, not a confirmed moderator
entries.product_use: Personalisation is a design hypothesis worth testing, not a selling point

entries.title: fMRI neurofeedback for the modulation of the neural networks associated with depression

outcomes.note: BOLD modulation and connectivity changes; effects region-specific

findings: Modulation occurred even in strategy-free protocols and within a single session
Learning effect increased over sessions
entries.product_use: Mechanistic context only; not a product protocol

entries.title: Neurofeedback to enhance sleep quality and insomnia: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials

outcomes.note: control conditions improved sleep quality more than neurofeedback

findings: No additional benefit of surface neurofeedback over diverse controls
Alpha-based protocols of 8-20 sessions were typical
entries.product_use: Sleep claims are unsupported for surface neurofeedback

entries.journal: Journal of the American Academy of Child & Adolescent Psychiatry
entries.title: Neurofeedback for Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder: Meta-Analysis of Clinical and Neuropsychological Outcomes From Randomized Controlled Trials

outcomes.note: not significant with probably blinded ratings or active/sham controls

findings: Only 4 studies directly assessed whether learning occurred
Risk of bias was unclear in most domains
limitations: Few trials used active or sham controls
entries.product_use: The unblinded effect is real but is not evidence of treatment efficacy

entries.journal: Journal of Child Psychology and Psychiatry
entries.title: Research Review: Pharmacological and non-pharmacological treatments for adolescents with attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder - a systematic review of the literature

outcomes.note: cognitive/behavioural treatments improved impairment and executive function consistently

findings: No intervention showed significant safety concerns
Long-term maintenance up to 3 years was shown for cognitive/behavioural treatments
Medication and cognitive/behavioural treatment effects appear complementary
limitations: Blinding is impossible for many treatments
entries.product_use: Position as a coping/function adjunct, never as a medication substitute

entries.title: Evaluating the evidence: a systematic review of reviews of the effectiveness and safety of digital interventions for ADHD

outcomes.note: inattention and executive function improved, but evidence quality was generally low
adverse effects reported in 8 of 26 reviews: physical discomfort, emotional reactions, behavioural issues including video-game addiction

findings: Adverse effects are inconsistently documented
Video games carried the most safety signals
entries.product_use: A safety monitoring plan is mandatory, especially for game-based delivery

entries.title: Treatments for ADHD in Children and Adolescents: A Systematic Review

outcomes.note: medication has the strongest evidence base but carries adverse events
many non-pharmacological treatments improve symptoms but with weaker evidence

findings: Few direct comparisons between alternative treatments exist
Medication plus psychosocial intervention did not systematically outperform monotherapy in the few combinations evaluated
entries.product_use: Comparator context for any ADHD-adjacent claim

entries.journal: The Australian and New Zealand Journal of Psychiatry
entries.title: Global prevalence of gaming disorder: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

outcomes.note: random-effects pooled estimate; 1.96% with stringent sampling; screening tool explains 77% of variance

findings: Worldwide pooled prevalence 3.05% (95% CI 2.38-3.91)
Estimates inflated by measurement and sampling: tool choice, adolescent samples, lower cut-offs, small samples
Male-to-female ratio about 2.5:1
entries.product_use: Set the safeguard base rate: a non-trivial minority develops disordered play, so rewards stay bounded, odds are disclosed, and the app never pushes more play.

entries.title: Prevalence of Internet gaming disorder in young adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

outcomes.note: gamer-only samples 8.1%; mixed samples 5.47%; instrument explains most variance

findings: Pooled IGD prevalence 6.1% (95% CI 5.03-7.40) in 18-35 year olds
Higher in gamer-only samples and rising over time in those samples
IGDS and DSM-5 criteria yield higher estimates than IGDT-10
entries.product_use: Young-adult heavy users carry the highest base rate; the daily break cue and session caps matter most for exactly this group.

entries.title: Burden of gaming disorder among adolescents: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

outcomes.note: prediction interval 1.0-48.1%; publication year positively associated with prevalence

findings: Pooled adolescent prevalence 8.6% (95% CI 6.9-10.8)
Increasing trend with publication year
Highest country estimate China at 11.7%
limitations: I2 of 100%; single-study countries report extreme values
Publication bias cannot be ruled out
entries.product_use: Adolescent prevalence near 9% and rising; Noesis serves adults, but the same structural caution applies to every reward feature it ships.

entries.title: Investigating gaming structural features associated with gaming disorder and proposing a revised taxonomical model: a scoping review.

outcomes.note: 105 articles; two risk classes: immersion/realism features and gambling-like reward-punishment features; intermittent rewards, near-miss, random-chance purchases and in-game currency implicated

findings: Social, narrative/identity and reward-punishment features dominate the evidence
Seven studies link random-chance purchases to disorder or proxies
Punishment features associate with willingness to continue via flow proxies
limitations: Scoping review: no quality appraisal or pooled effects
entries.product_use: Avoid gambling-like structural features entirely (no random-chance content, no currency); keep intermittent rewards cosmetic and near-miss cues real.

entries.title: Risk and protective factors for (internet) gaming disorder: a meta-analysis of pre-COVID studies.

outcomes.note: 1586 effects; moderately strong heterogeneous risk factors: male gender, depression, impulsivity, anxiety, stress, gaming time, escape motivation
few robust protective factors with markedly smaller effects: self-esteem, life satisfaction, education

findings: Numerous moderately strong but heterogeneous risk factors
Only a few empirically robust protective factors, all small
Bias adjustments modest; measurement and reporting practices weak
limitations: Heterogeneous measures of the same constructs
entries.product_use: Design for the protective side (competence, self-esteem, satisfying framing) and guard the risk correlates: impulsivity, anxiety, escape motivation and long sessions.

entries.title: Internet gaming disorder, attention deficit hyperactivity disorder and learning in adults: a systematic review.

outcomes.note: inattention and hyperactivity-impulsivity associated with IGD incidence and severity; five mediators proposed (mental health, gender, culture, motivation/game type, habits)

findings: ADHD symptoms consistently associated with IGD incidence and severity
Comorbid users show more depression/anxiety, lower self-control
IGD negatively linked to academic performance in adults with ADHD
limitations: Mostly cross-sectional: no causal mediation established
entries.product_use: Users with attention difficulties are more vulnerable to compulsive play: keep risk opt-in with default bank, keep cool-off paths short, never frame training as ADHD treatment.

entries.title: Photic- and pattern-induced seizures: expert consensus of the Epilepsy Foundation of America Working Group.

outcomes.note: 15-25 Hz most provocative; luminance, red-flash and stripe-density limits specified with screening guidance

findings: Expert consensus on provocative stimulus parameters for photosensitive seizures
Screening and stimulus limits specified for visual content
limitations: Consensus statement, not a pooled effect
entries.product_use: Screen for photosensitivity before any flashing content; enforce luminance, frequency, red-flash and stripe-density limits with an emergency stop.

entries.title: Photic- and pattern-induced seizures: a review for the Epilepsy Foundation of America Working Group.

outcomes.note: photosensitivity affects 0.3-3%; pattern and geometry sensitivity documented

findings: Photosensitivity prevalence and provocative pattern characteristics reviewed
Companion evidence base to the 2005 consensus statement
entries.product_use: Ground the photosensitivity screen in the prevalence base rate and pattern-sensitivity evidence, not in generic caution.

entries.title: Visually-provoked seizures: Consensus of the Epilepsy Foundation Working Group.

outcomes.note: updated consensus on visually-provoked seizures; screening before flashing or high-contrast content

findings: Updated working-group consensus superseding the 2005 statements
Confirms screening and stimulus-limit approach
limitations: Consensus statement, not a pooled effect
entries.product_use: Keep the R14/R15 safety layer current: the 2026 consensus reaffirms pre-exposure screening and hard stimulus limits.

entries.title: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Gamification on Physical Activity: Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.

outcomes.note: Hedges g vs active and inactive controls; generalises across age and health status
follow-up averaging 14 weeks after the intervention: very small sustained effect

findings: Gamified interventions beat both inactive and nongamified active controls
Effects persist weakly after the intervention, arguing against a pure novelty effect
entries.product_use: Gamification moves behaviour while active but fades after: use game elements for session initiation and adherence, never as the outcome; re-earn attention each session.

entries.title: Evaluation of the Effectiveness of Behavioral Economic Incentive Programs for Goal Achievement on Healthy Diet, Weight Control and Physical Activity: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-analysis.

outcomes.note: deposit contracts vs no incentive for activity goal achievement; 35 RCTs
only deposit persisted at follow-up; lottery faded

findings: Deposit contracts ranked best at program end and were the only design with effects persisting after the program
Lottery and standard incentives worked during the program but faded
entries.product_use: Deposit-style stakes beat lotteries and persist: the engagement arm stakes symbolic momentum attendance-contingently, all-or-nothing, framed as gain.

entries.title: The effectiveness of financial incentives for health behaviour change: systematic review and meta-analysis.

outcomes.note: all behaviours combined vs usual care; smoking cessation RR 2.48 short-term

findings: Incentives beat usual care across behaviours while active
Effects fade beyond three months after incentive removal
entries.product_use: Incentives work while active and fade after: re-earn attention each session; never promise lasting change from rewards alone.

entries.title: The utility of monetary contingency contracts for weight loss: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

outcomes.note: small-to-medium effect of contingency contracts during treatment and on retention; no post-treatment effect

findings: Contingency contracts promote goal completion and retention while active
Self-set deposits, non-lump-sum payment and all-or-nothing refunds work best
entries.product_use: All-or-nothing, attendance-contingent refunds aid retention: stake on finishing, not on scoring; self-set terms work best.

entries.title: What Effect Do Goal Setting Interventions Have on Physical Activity and Psychological Outcomes in Insufficiently Active Adults? A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

outcomes.note: specific goals in insufficiently active adults; unrewarded goals beat rewarded ones (g 1.30 vs 0.60)

findings: Specific goals have a large effect on activity in insufficiently active adults
Goals without rewards outperform goals with rewards
limitations: Only specific goals studied; no comparison of goal types
Range of goal types not investigated
entries.product_use: Weekly goal is specific, few, and unrewarded: set an explicit session count, never pay for it, and let the goal itself do the work.

entries.title: The effectiveness of multi-component goal setting interventions for changing physical activity behaviour: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

outcomes.note: multi-component goal setting vs no-goal controls; daily and combined daily-weekly goals beat weekly-only

findings: Medium positive effect of goal-setting interventions across diverse populations
Daily and combined daily-plus-weekly goals work; weekly-only goals lose the effect
entries.product_use: Pair the per-session intention (daily) with the weekly goal: the combination is the supported configuration, not weekly goals alone.

entries.title: Impact of implementation intentions on physical activity practice in adults: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials.

outcomes.note: if-then planning with reinforcement in adults including cardiac, diabetic and sedentary samples

findings: Implementation intentions with reinforcement increase activity practice
Action planning plus coping planning is the effective bundle
entries.product_use: The when-where plan needs reinforcement to work: the weekly goal and summary are the reinforcement loop around the intention.

entries.title: The effect of testing versus restudy on retention: a meta-analytic review of the testing effect.

outcomes.note: testing vs restudy; 81% of effects positive; initial recall tests yield the largest benefits

findings: Testing reliably beats restudy for retention (g=0.50)
Effortful initial recall drives the benefit; feedback helps
entries.product_use: Every block is a test with feedback, not a re-read: the app core loop is retrieval practice, and testing beats restudy especially with effortful recall plus feedback.

entries.title: Distributed practice in verbal recall tasks: A review and quantitative synthesis.

outcomes.note: 839 assessments in 317 experiments; spaced beats massed at every retention interval; optimal gap rises with retention interval; ~15% benefit distributing across days

findings: Spaced beats massed at every retention interval from minutes to months
Distributing learning across days markedly improves retention; cramming within a day impairs it
entries.product_use: Count practice days, not sessions: distributing learning across days markedly improves retention; cramming within a day does not.

entries.title: Time to Form a Habit: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Health Behaviour Habit Formation and Its Determinants.

outcomes.note: habit-score improvement pre-post; medians 59-66 days to formation; morning and self-selected habits stronger

findings: Habit strength improves with intervention across behaviours
Formation takes about two months to start, with wide individual variation
entries.product_use: Habits take about two months to start forming: the calendar shows the accumulation. Morning and self-selected practice strengthen formation.

entries.title: A systematic review and meta-analysis of applications of the Self-Report Habit Index to nutrition and physical activity behaviours.

outcomes.note: habit strength correlates with behavioural frequency; habit moderates the intention-behaviour relation

findings: Medium-to-strong habit-behaviour correlation across health behaviours
Context-dependent repetition is the formation mechanism
entries.product_use: Same context, repeated: the stable when-where plan plus daily repetition is the automaticity engine; a single miss does not reset formation.

entries.title: A systematic review of gamification in e-Health.

outcomes.note: mostly short-term engagement through extrinsic rewards; weak empirical evidence for behaviour change

findings: Gamification in e-Health drives short-term engagement via extrinsic rewards
Empirical evidence for sustained behaviour change is weak
entries.product_use: Temper the gamification case: rewards drive session initiation, not proven behaviour change; never pay for outcomes.
